source: JZ Mock A · Paper 2 · Question 20 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock A · Paper 2 · Question 20
knowledgePattern: Retain the domain while counting squared trigonometric branches on an open-ended interval
solution:
Both numerators are nonnegative. Each denominator is nonnegative but must not vanish, so exclude sinx=1 and sin2x=1. On the remaining domain the fractions are nonnegative and both denominators positive, making squaring and cross-multiplication reversible.

The equation becomes (1+sinx)(1−sinx)=(1+sin2x)(1−sin2x), so sin2x=sin22x. Using sin2x=2sinxcosx, this is sin2x(1−4cos2x)=0.

Thus sinx=0 or cosx=1/2 or cosx=−1/2. Together these are exactly the multiples of 60∘. None makes either original denominator zero, so every listed angle is valid.

The nonnegative roots are 0∘,60∘,120∘,…. The sixteenth is 900∘, and the seventeenth is 960∘. Since the upper bound is strict, the smallest integer p including the sixteenth root is 901. Answer F.

hints.body: Find the inputs that make either denominator zero, and check the signs of the fractions on the remaining domain.
hints.recap: Squaring preserves candidates only when the original signs and denominator restrictions are checked.
hints.pitfall: A zero denominator remains excluded even if later algebra cancels it.

hints.title: Count from the included starting endpoint
hints.body: Order the valid roots over a complete period, extend the pattern, and locate the required root by its position in the list.
hints.recap: Root counts must respect interval endpoints and count coincident branches only once.
hints.pitfall: The root at the starting endpoint, if valid, is already the first root.
hints.pause: Use the strict upper inequality to choose the smallest permitted integer.
